text:
megan_ae: FYI - AuroraBank wants a Private POC. Requirements: no public ingress, egress must be allowlisted to their partners & audit team, HSM-backed KMS, and SOC wants original client IPs. Also they require FIPS endpoints for cryptographic compliance. Need guidance on connectivity: PrivateLink vs TGW/Peering vs running small nodes in their account. Also need firewall lines and a quick cost delta vs Dedicated.

rory_se: are they multi-account? steady RPS + burst? Any Direct Connect or DX already?

megan_ae: single account now, may go multi later. Steady ~70 rps, bursts to ~450. They have Direct Connect + DX gateway but prefer security ops to control egress. They insist on fixed outbound IPs for partner allowlists and FIPS KMS.

jiwoo_arch: quick take:
- PrivateLink (NLB + VPCE): best for "no public ingress". Keeps our infra in our VPC and exposes a service endpoint in theirs. Easier signoff for security teams, but not transitive.
- TGW/Peering: good when they want L3 access to multiple subnets or want us to place nodes in their account. Requires CIDR planning and longer review.
- Bring-your-own-nodes (deploy small autoscaling nodes in their account): gives them full control over egress EIPs and KMS usage (if we encrypt with customer CMKs). Operationally heavier for us.

jiwoo_arch: additional note on preserving client IPs:
- NLB with proxy protocol v2 can forward original IP to backends if you control the NLB/targets. VPCE to NLB usually preserves source but health/proxy behavior depends on target type. In practice, the cleanest pattern is customer-hosted egress proxy (small NGINX/HAProxy) with EIP so SOC has the external IP and we preserve X-Forwarded-For.

denise_netops: firewall snippet they can paste:

```
# AuroraBank egress rules for Redwood POC
- Protocol: TCP
- Ports: 443
- Destination: <VPCE CIDR block OR list of Redwood EIPs provided in advance>
- Description: Redwood private endpoints / egress
# If NLB healthchecks are used, allow TCP 8443 (confirm exact port list with Redwood ops)
```

denise_netops: on fixed IPs: options are (1) customer-provided EIP + egress proxy (recommended), (2) Redwood publishes a small EIP set (requires procurement & ops cadence), or (3) run nodes in their account and assign their NAT EIPs (we bill infra in their account). For FIPS/KMS, we can integrate with customer CMKs (requires IAM and KMS grant setup).

rory_se: pricing (very rough scoping):
- Dedicated: predictable monthly commit. Example: 4x GPU reserved pool estimate ~$10k-15k/month; 8x GPU ~$18k-25k/month depending on model.
- Private (customer infra): platform onboarding fee ~$25k-40k one-time + annual platform support ~$8k-15k; customer pays infra costs (EC2/GPU/NAT/EIPs). Exact quote from finance.

security-bot: reminder: attach security questionnaire and request KMS/HSM & log retention answers.

megan_ae: next steps: scheduling 30m tech handoff with AuroraBank + netops tomorrow 8:30am PT. @jiwoo_arch @denise_netops can you join? I'll request their proposed outbound EIPs and CIDR list beforehand.

jiwoo_arch: can do.

denise_netops: available. 

megan_ae: thanks all :white_check_mark: I'll post notes after the call.
